question: What are the standard payment terms for a rice export deal under HS 1006?
answer: Standard payment terms for HS 1006 (rice) export deals are typically 30% advance via escrow hold and 70% against shipping documents released after QC pass [1]. Suppliers on the approved panel default to a Letter of Credit at sight when the deal value exceeds $50,000, falling back to escrow-guard milestone releases below that threshold [2].

sources.title: Rice HS1006 Trade Playbook
sources.content: For HS 1006 rice shipments, the recommended payment structure is 30% advance payment held in escrow at PI acceptance, with the remaining 70% released against shipping documents (Bill of Lading, Certificate of Origin, QC pass certificate) once SGS inspection clears. This structure balances supplier cash-flow needs against buyer risk on quality non-conformance.

sources.title: Supplier Terms Glossary
sources.content: Letter of Credit (LC) at sight: default instrument for deals above $50,000 with approved-panel suppliers. Below that threshold, escrow-guard milestone releases (advance + on-QC + on-dispatch) are preferred for lower transaction overhead and faster supplier payout cycles.
